evidence: Commit message: 'The prohibition therefore now reaches a builder added in a NEW module or moved between modules, cases the hard-coded pair silently missed.'

ABSENCE: the only teeth test (test_direct_routing_reader_detector_has_teeth) drives _is_direct_reader_violation on inline source, not _projection_builders()'s tree scan; no test injects a synthetic offending builder in an un-gate-listed llm module and asserts it appears in `offenders`.

test_no_projection_builder_reads_raw_routing_directly only asserts the two named gates are present and that the real tree is clean (`assert not offenders`), which cannot detect discovery that silently misses a non-gate module.
advisory.finding: The newly-introduced whole-tree discovery guard (_projection_builders scanning all of src/rebar/llm) has no teeth test proving it CATCHES a raw-routing-reading DiscoveryStagePlan builder in a module OUTSIDE the two names in _PROJECTION_BUILDER_GATES — which the commit message states is the entire reason for the rewrite ('now reaches a builder added in a NEW module or moved between modules, cases the hard-coded pair silently missed'). The existing teeth test only exercises _is_direct_reader_violation on synthetic source; the tree-scan path is asserted only against the current clean tree, so a regression that narrowed discovery back to the named gates would pass unnoticed.
scenarios: A future edit narrows _projection_builders back to hand-listed paths or breaks _constructs_discovery_stage for a new construction form; the clean-tree assertion still passes and the widened reach is silently lost.
